title: Michigan vs. Illinois Weed: Prices, Taxes and Limits
h1: Michigan vs. Illinois Cannabis: What Chicago-Area Shoppers Should Know
metaDescription: Michigan vs. Illinois weed compared: taxes, limits for visitors, prices, home grow, where you can consume and why nothing can cross the state line.
excerpt: Taxes, limits, home grow and consumption rules side by side for Chicago-area adults, plus the one constant: buy and enjoy in Michigan, never carry it home.
keyTakeaways: Michigan adds a flat 10% excise plus 6% sales tax; Illinois charges a 10%, 20% or 25% excise by product, plus state and local taxes.
In Michigan, one transaction can include up to 2.5 ounces for any adult 21 or older, with a 15-gram cap on concentrate.
Michigan adults may cultivate as many as 12 plants per residence; in Illinois, home grow is for registered medical patients only.
Federal law bars taking cannabis across any state line, and the route home crosses Indiana, where possessing cannabis is a crime.
body:
Comparing Michigan vs. Illinois weed rules comes down to a few points. Michigan's retail taxes are simpler and, for most products, lower. Any adult 21 or older can buy the same amount in Michigan whether they live here or not, and neither state allows use in public places. One thing never changes: what you buy in Michigan stays in Michigan. Here's the side-by-side, as of October 2026.

## Why Chicago-Area Shoppers Compare the Two States

Southwest Michigan is an easy drive from Chicago, and our New Buffalo store, close to the Indiana border, is a convenient stop on the way in. Both states let adults 21 and older buy from licensed stores, but taxes, limits and home grow differ. This guide is general information, not legal advice; our [Michigan cannabis law guide](/cannabis-laws-by-state/michigan/) and [Illinois law guide](/cannabis-laws-by-state/illinois/) go deeper.

## Michigan vs. Illinois Weed Taxes, Side by Side

The Michigan cannabis tax at the register is simple. Adult-use sales get a 10% excise, then the 6% sales tax is applied to the price with the excise already added. Ring up $100 of product and you'll pay $10 of excise plus $6.60 of sales tax, for $116.60 at the register. Registered medical patients pay only the sales tax.

The Illinois cannabis tax rate depends on the product. Cannabis at or below 35% THC, which covers most flower, is taxed at 10%. Infused products such as edibles are taxed at 20%. Cannabis above 35% THC is taxed at 25%, the tier where most vape oils and concentrates land. Illinois then adds its 6.25% state sales tax, plus local sales taxes and any county or city cannabis taxes.

| | Michigan | Illinois |
|---|---|---|
| Excise on adult-use purchases | 10% on everything | 10%, 20% or 25%, by product type and THC level |
| Sales tax | 6%, figured on the price plus excise | 6.25% state rate, plus local sales and cannabis taxes |
| Medical purchases | 6% sales tax only, no excise | Taxed at Illinois' lower rate for qualifying drugs |

The upshot: for edibles, vapes and concentrates, the same shelf price costs noticeably more at an Illinois register. For lower-THC flower the base rates are close, and Illinois' local add-ons set the gap.

## Prices and Product Variety

Shelf prices change constantly with harvests, promotions and product type, so blanket price comparisons go stale fast. Taxes are the predictable part; for the rest, compare current menus before you drive. Licensed stores in both states offer the familiar formats: flower, pre-rolls, vapes, concentrates, edibles, drinks and topicals. What's on a given shelf varies by store and by week. Ordering ahead lets you choose before you arrive; see [how to order cannabis online](/blog/how-to-order-cannabis-online/).

## Possession and Purchase Limits for Residents and Visitors

Michigan doesn't split its limits by residency. Any adult 21 or older may buy, carry and transport as much as 2.5 ounces, of which concentrate can make up 15 grams at most. A single transaction at a licensed store can't exceed that amount, and before every sale the store checks a valid photo ID proving you're at least 21.

Illinois does split them. The Illinois possession limit for non-residents is half the resident limit:

| | Illinois residents | Visitors to Illinois |
|---|---|---|
| Cannabis flower | 60 grams | 30 grams |
| THC in infused products | 1,000 mg | 500 mg |
| Concentrate | 10 grams | 5 grams |

A mix of products is fine in Illinois, as long as each category stays within its own limit.

## Home Grow and Medical Programs Compared

Adults 21 and older in Michigan may cultivate as many as 12 plants for personal use, capped at 12 per residence. The plants have to stay hidden from public view and locked away. In Illinois, only registered medical cannabis patients may grow at home, up to five plants.

Both states tax medical purchases more lightly, as the table above shows. Michigan law also recognizes out-of-state medical cards. A visiting patient can shop at a licensed medical provisioning center by presenting a valid, unexpired card along with photo ID. Not every store serves visiting patients, so ask first.

## Where You Can Consume in Each State

Neither state allows cannabis use in public places. In Michigan, landlords and property managers can prohibit smoking or use on their premises, and on-site consumption exists only where the local government has authorized it. Illinois applies its Smoke Free Illinois Act to cannabis smoke and lets local governments authorize consumption lounges.

On the road, Michigan forbids using cannabis while you drive, and smoking it anywhere in the passenger compartment on a public road. In Illinois, cannabis riding in a moving vehicle must stay sealed in its original packaging, inside a container that's odor-proof and child-resistant. In Michigan, plan on a private residence where you have permission. Our guide to [where you can smoke in Michigan](/blog/where-can-you-smoke-weed-in-michigan/) has the details.

## Can You Bring Weed From Michigan to Illinois? The State Line and Indiana

No. Federal law still makes it illegal to take cannabis from one state into another, even when both have legalized it. Illinois' official guidance also tells people not to carry cannabis over state lines. Because Illinois and Michigan share no land border, the drive between them crosses northwest Indiana.

Indiana has legalized neither adult-use nor medical marijuana, so holding any amount there is a crime. For someone with no prior drug conviction, the charge is a Class B misdemeanor, punishable by up to 180 days in jail and a fine of up to $1,000. A legal Michigan receipt doesn't change that.

The plan that works: buy what you'll use during your stay, enjoy it where it's allowed and head home with none in the car. Leftovers can be finished or given to another adult 21 or older in Michigan, with nothing received in return. Our standing reminder applies to every purchase: don't travel across state lines with cannabis, and never drive after consuming.

## Buying Weed in Michigan From Chicago? Plan a New Buffalo Stop

High Society New Buffalo is near the Indiana border, a short drive off I-94 at Exit 1 (M-239), on the US-12 corridor.

- Bring valid government photo ID. Out-of-state IDs are usually fine at our New Buffalo store.
- Ordering ahead? Choose in-store or curbside pickup, and watch for a text when a curbside order is waiting.
- Parking is free on site, and most visits take under 10 minutes. Weekends and late afternoons tend to be the busiest times.
- Cash works here; other ways to pay differ by store.

See the [New Buffalo store page](/dispensary-locations/new-buffalo/) for hours, directions and the menu, and our [New Buffalo trip guide for Chicago visitors](/blog/visiting-new-buffalo-from-chicago-cannabis/) for planning the drive.

faq.q: Is weed cheaper in Michigan than Illinois?
faq.a: At the register, usually yes. Michigan adds a flat 10% excise plus 6% sales tax, while Illinois charges a 10%, 20% or 25% excise by product, plus state and local taxes. Shelf prices change constantly and vary by store, so compare current menus rather than anyone's price list.

faq.q: Can Illinois residents buy cannabis in Michigan?
faq.a: Yes. Michigan's adult-use law applies to anyone 21 or older, not just residents. Bring valid government photo ID; out-of-state IDs usually work at our New Buffalo store. The 2.5-ounce per-transaction limit is the same for everyone.

faq.q: Can I bring cannabis from Michigan back to Illinois?
faq.a: No. Even between two states that have both legalized it, moving cannabis over the line breaks federal law, and Illinois' guidance says not to do it. The drive home also passes through Indiana, and having any amount of cannabis there is a crime. Enjoy your purchase in Michigan and head home with none in the car.

faq.q: How much cannabis can a visitor buy in Michigan?
faq.a: The same as a resident: up to 2.5 ounces per transaction for anyone 21 or older, of which concentrate can be 15 grams at most. Plan to use it in Michigan, since none of it can legally travel home with you.
